thesis_statement: RTX pairs the two most durable aerospace and defense franchises - commercial aftermarket (Collins + Pratt spares and repair) and defense programs of record - under one $289B backlog (+22% YoY), delivering 16% organic growth with margin expansion across all three segments and a raised full-year outlook.

base.summary: Backlog converts at the raised 8-9% organic pace with adjusted EPS of $7.10-7.25 and free cash flow near $8.6B; the dual-engine structure smooths any single-demand shock.
drivers: raised FY26 outlook: adjusted sales $95-96B, adjusted EPS $7.10-7.25, FCF $8.50-8.75B

bull.summary: Commercial air traffic growth and fleet aging keep aftermarket pricing firm while European and Pacific rearmament expand defense backlog; margins expand past prior peaks.
drivers: margin expansion across all three segments
Blue Canyon divestiture ($620M) sharpening the portfolio

bear.summary: Air-traffic or airline-capex cyclicality cuts commercial OE (+26% is the cyclical part), defense budget priorities shift, and the acquisition-accounting EPS drag persists.
drivers: GAAP EPS ($1.57) runs $0.32 below adjusted ($1.89) on acquisition accounting and restructuring

key_risks: GAAP-adjusted gap: $0.27 of acquisition accounting and $0.05 of restructuring drag on quarterly EPS; judge adjusted trends but watch the gap's persistence.
Commercial OE growth (+26% at Collins) is the cyclical component; the durable economics are in aftermarket and defense.
Net debt ~$30.6B with continued capacity investment; balance sheet is fine but not fortress.
Government-budget and export-licensing risk on the defense side (geopolitics-dependent in both directions).
